environment.policy: one performance workload at a time; independent truth outside cgroup

limits: census checks primary keys, categories and independently regenerated norms; it does not project and compare every vector coordinate
pre-ready SIGKILL is verified; there is no internal recovery progress hook
full workflow has no per-request deadline and is not a formal time-limit pass
memory.peak includes file cache; sampled anon/file maxima are not additive
phase T excludes external oracle generation; no phase weights are invented

config.cache_policy: private copy; Sync/FADV_DONTNEED/mincore before startup and again after ready before each SQL group
config.census_validation: all primary keys, c9 categories, independent vector norms; not elementwise vectors
config.timing: startup from before exec; query protocol/output only; truth generation and response decode outside query T

fallback_engine.environment_evidence_limit: run.py fallback supplies MVDB_NO_AVXVNNI=1; this historical log does not snapshot env. The log verifies both AVX-VNNI kernel tests were unavailable/skipped and engine tests passed.

selected_tests.identity_limit: Historical command logs identify candidate source/binary paths, without before/after SHA snapshots; selected stress SHA is separately verified.

environment_incident.root_cause: Undetermined. Low free space on the Windows host D: drive was observed after failure, but there is no retained kernel evidence proving ENOSPC or a device error caused the read-only filesystem.

procedure: Copied source snapshots, binaries, results and STATE.json over WSL UNC and verified all file SHA-256 hashes.
Terminated the failed test distribution; copied its VHDX to C: without modifying or deleting the D: original.
Registered copied VHDX as ArchBenchRound7; filesystem mounted read-write without manual repair or remount.
Verified all 787 rescued file hashes again in the recovered distribution.
Started a fresh complete stress workflow using a new label and directory; original failed evidence remains byte-for-byte archived.

environment_incident.interpretation: The recovered run is a capacity/exact/transaction/crash-recovery check. Its T/B/M must not be pooled with the original interleaved performance comparisons because host storage changed.
